transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I came in because my sleep has gotten really messed up. I work overnight shifts, and even after I get off, I’ll just lie there wide awake. Then if I finally do fall asleep, I wake up scared, and it feels like I didn’t rest at all.
Do your sleep problems happen mainly on days when you’re working overnight shifts?
Mostly, yeah. It’s worst after I get off an overnight shift. I’ll be exhausted but still just lie there wide awake, and if I finally do fall asleep, I wake up scared and don’t feel rested at all.
When you wake up scared, is it because of a frightening dream?
I don’t always remember a dream. It’s more like I finally drift off after lying there awake, and then I wake up scared anyway, like I didn’t really sleep or rest.
When you wake up scared, do you remember having a bad dream?
Not usually, no. I don’t really remember a bad dream most of the time. It’s more like I finally drift off after lying there wide awake, and then I wake up scared anyway, like I never actually rested.
On days when you’re not working overnight shifts, does your sleep get better?

A little, but not really back to normal. It’s mainly bad after overnight shifts, but my sleep still feels broken up. I’ll be exhausted and still wide awake, and when I do sleep, I wake up scared and feel like I didn’t rest.
Do you work during the hours when you would normally be asleep?

Yes. I work overnight shifts, so I’m up during the hours I’d normally be sleeping. Then when I get off, I’ll still lie there wide awake, and if I do drift off, I wake up scared and feel like I didn’t rest at all.
Before you started working overnight shifts, did you already have trouble sleeping?

I mean, I came in because my sleep is all broken up now. After the overnight shifts is when it’s really bad—I’ll get off and still just lie there wide awake. Then if I do finally fall asleep, I wake up scared and feel like I never really rested.
Did these sleep problems start after you began working overnight shifts?

Yeah, it really got bad with the overnight shifts. I’ll get off work and be exhausted, but I still just lie there awake. Then if I finally do fall asleep, I wake up scared and it feels like I didn’t rest at all.
When you have several days off and can sleep at night instead of during the day, does your sleep return to normal?
Not really. Even when I’ve got time off, my sleep still feels broken up. I’ll lie there wide awake, and if I do finally drift off, I wake up scared and feel like I didn’t rest.
When you wake up scared, do you feel a sudden rush of panic?
I wake up scared, yeah… I don’t know if it’s like a sudden rush of panic exactly. I just know I come awake feeling afraid, and then I don’t feel rested at all.
When you wake up scared, does your heart feel like it’s pounding?
I’m not really sure. I wake up scared, but I haven’t really noticed if my heart is pounding or not.
When you wake up scared, are you unable to move?
I don’t think it’s that I can’t move. I just wake up scared, and my sleep’s already been so broken up that I feel like I never really rested.
When you wake up scared, does it feel like sudden intense terror?
I don’t know if I’d call it sudden intense terror. I just wake up scared, and my sleep is so broken up that even when I do sleep, I feel like I never rested.
When you wake up scared, do you remember a dream?
I don’t really remember a dream most times. I just know I drift off for a little bit, then wake up scared, and after that it feels like I never really slept at all.
Do you feel very sleepy while you’re at work during your overnight shifts?

Yeah… I do feel worn out, but it’s more like my sleep is all broken up. I get off the overnight shift and I’ll still be lying there wide awake, and then if I do fall asleep I wake up scared. So I end up feeling like I never really rested.
Do you find yourself actually falling asleep when you need to stay awake?

Not really falling asleep on the job, no. It’s more that I’m exhausted because my sleep is so broken up. I get off the overnight shift and still can’t sleep, and then when I finally do, I wake up scared and feel like I didn’t rest at all.
If you stopped working overnight shifts for a while, do you think your sleep would still be a problem?

I think it probably would still be a problem. The overnight shifts make it worse, but even when I get home and should be able to sleep, I just lie there wide awake. Then if I finally drift off, I wake up scared and it feels like I never really rested.
When you try to sleep, do you usually have trouble falling asleep?

Yeah, I do. I’ll get off my overnight shift and think I should be able to sleep, but I just lie there wide awake. And then when I finally do drift off, I wake up scared, so it doesn’t feel like I really rested.
On a period when you are not working overnight shifts at all, do you still have trouble falling asleep?
Yeah… even when I’m not on overnights, I still have trouble falling asleep. I’ll be exhausted, but I just lie there wide awake, and if I do finally drift off, I wake up scared and don’t feel rested.
